samples.summary: The revocation reconcile deletes entries holding un-pushed changes with no archive, unlike every other delete path
samples.evidence: `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` loops `store.purgeDocument(id, { archives: "drop", skipOpen: true, updatedSince })` for every stored id absent from the server listing. `purgeDocument` → `purge()` deletes the snapshot, header and the **whole change log** unconditionally; it never consults `changeCount(key)`. Eviction (`evictOldest`, wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1468) treats a non-empty log as sacred precisely because "this store cannot tell an acked change from an unacked one … being wrong the other way costs a document that is silently no longer there", and `remove()` archives on a loss. This path does neither. It deletes on an *absence* from a single listing, so any transient reason a document is missing from `GET /documents` (a membership row not yet visible, a document mid-move between workspaces, a backend that ever starts paginating) permanently destroys the only durable copy of unsent work, with nothing archived and nothing told to the user. The two existing guards do not cover it: `skipOpen` only spares a document some tab has open right now, and `updatedSince` only spares entries touched after the listing was requested — a document edited offline yesterday and closed satisfies neither.

samples.summary: The durable client's WafflebaseDocStore is created in useMemo and never closed, leaking an IndexedDB connection per mounted editor
samples.evidence: `const store = useMemo(() => new WafflebaseDocStore({...}), [userId])` with no `useEffect(() => () => store.close(), [store])` anywhere in the file (grep for `close()` in durable-yorkie-provider.tsx returns no matches). `WafflebaseDocStore.close()` exists and is documented as needed "so a `deleteDatabase` elsewhere is not blocked", and `OfflineRuntime` does call it on unmount (offline-runtime.tsx:208). Every durable document opened in a session therefore leaves an open IDBDatabase connection behind for the life of the tab; those connections also block another tab's version upgrade until `onversionchange` fires.

samples.summary: The lapse chain falls through to "another-tab" for causes that are not another tab, producing a false tooltip
samples.evidence: `const lapse = decided?.durable ? undefined : !supportsClientKey() ? "unsupported" : !permitted ? "not-permitted" : !offlineEnabled ? "not-enabled" : "another-tab"`. Every remaining non-durable cause lands on `"another-tab"`, including: no resolved identity (`person` undefined — the branch at line 351 explicitly falls back to `inner` on `!person`), a `pdf-` document excluded by `isExcluded()` in use-durable-document.ts, and a `standDown()` that demoted the document after the SDK refused the attach. The tooltip then asserts "This document is open in another tab, and that tab is the one saving it to this device" (sync-status-tooltip.ts LAPSE_REASONS) when no other tab exists, which is exactly the misdiagnosis the per-cause table was added to prevent.

samples.summary: The fallback store built inside the disable watcher is never closed
samples.evidence: `const current = store() ?? new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId: who });` then `void eraseOfflineData(current, who).catch(...)`. When the fallback branch is taken (the documented common case — Settings is the one route with no editor mounted, so `store()` may be the runtime's store, but on any path where it is `undefined` a fresh store is built), nothing ever calls `close()` on it. The connection stays open for the life of the tab and can block a later version upgrade.

samples.summary: `standDown` performs an external side effect (releasing the Web Lock) inside a setState updater, which React may invoke more than once
samples.evidence: `setDecision((current) => { if (!current?.session) return current; current.session.release(); return { subject: current.subject }; })`. Updaters must be pure; React StrictMode double-invokes them and React may re-run an updater during a rebase. It happens to be safe today only because `DurableSession.release()` latches on a private `released` flag (durable-session.ts), so a second call is a no-op — but that is an accident of the other module's implementation, and a double-decrement of `entry.holders` would free a lock name a later tab has since taken, handing two tabs the same stable client key. The release belongs in an effect or a plain callback, not in the updater.

samples.summary: The module-level `evictedKeys` set grows without bound for the life of the tab
samples.evidence: `evictedFor(dbName)` returns a process-lifetime `Set<string>` that `collectStale`, `dropAllForUser`, `purgeDocument` and `evictOldest` all add to, and only `saveSnapshot` ever removes from (line 636). A thirty-day sweep that collects hundreds of another account's keys adds every one of them permanently, since nothing will ever write a fresh snapshot under those keys in this tab. Bounded by the tab's lifetime, so the cost is small, but it is unbounded growth with no eviction of its own.

finding.summary: The revocation reconcile deletes entries holding un-pushed changes with no archive, unlike every other delete path
finding.evidence: `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` loops `store.purgeDocument(id, { archives: "drop", skipOpen: true, updatedSince })` for every stored id absent from the server listing. `purgeDocument` → `purge()` deletes the snapshot, header and the **whole change log** unconditionally; it never consults `changeCount(key)`. Eviction (`evictOldest`, wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1468) treats a non-empty log as sacred precisely because "this store cannot tell an acked change from an unacked one … being wrong the other way costs a document that is silently no longer there", and `remove()` archives on a loss. This path does neither. It deletes on an *absence* from a single listing, so any transient reason a document is missing from `GET /documents` (a membership row not yet visible, a document mid-move between workspaces, a backend that ever starts paginating) permanently destroys the only durable copy of unsent work, with nothing archived and nothing told to the user. verdict.reason: The claimed code exists exactly as described. purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments (offline-erase.ts:491-497) calls purgeDocument(id, {archives:"drop", skipOpen:true, updatedSince:listedAt}) for every stored id absent from GET /documents; purgeDocument (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:923-939) applies only the isLive and updatedAt guards, then purge() (865-873) unconditionally deletes snapshot, header and the entire CHANGES range with no changeCount check and no archive write. That contrasts with remove(), which archives the change rows before deleting (829-849), and evictOldest, which skips any doc whose changeCount > 0 (1468), and with the documented 401 policy of erasing nothing because a live entry carries the un-pushed log. No caller-side or store-side guard spares an entry holding a non-empty un-pushed log: offline-runtime.tsx:135-164 supplies only listedAt and isOpenElsewhere, so a document edited offline and since closed satisfies neither. A deletion or workspace move the device never reopened therefore destroys the only durable copy of unsent work silently, with no archive and no user notice - data loss on a reachable path, squarely in the correctness lane. Only the framing "unlike every other delete path" is loose, since purgeOfflineDocuments (403-407) also drops live change logs without archiving; that does not undercut the substantive defect, and the design doc's own rules (line 285 "keeping its archive", goal line 54-55) make the silent loss a gap rather than sanctioned behaviour.
